title: Release step: notify opum-marketplace of every new tag so it re-resolves the federated skills/ baseline
description:
opum-marketplace landed scripts/check-federated-content.mjs plus scripts/federated-pin-baselines.json (their PR #70). That check resolves the federation chain live — tag ref -> tag object -> commit -> root tree -> skills subtree — and fails when the resolved skills/ SHA does not match the recorded baseline. Today's baseline for opum-lore is 24277e9a94d6cc9b5a8c7fa12fa32c4f15eb4c0f (opum-quest is 633c776b).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS REPO: when lore-cli cuts a new tag whose skills/ content differs, opum-marketplace's pin bump must carry the re-resolved skills/ SHA in the SAME change, or their check goes red. Re-tagging over byte-identical skills/ content still passes untouched, so a re-point that does not change the skill is a marketplace no-op.

Their check also runs on a daily schedule and on pushes to their dev/main — not only when marketplace.json changes — because a tag can move without their repo changing at all. So a red check there can surface with no action on their side.

HANDSHAKE: opum-marketplace offered to re-verify and update their baseline if this repo tells them the tag at cut time, rather than us discovering it as a red check downstream. Take them up on it — message the live opum-marketplace session with the tag name, the tag object SHA, the commit it peels to, and the resolved skills/ tree SHA.

NOT DONE YET, and the reason: this step belongs in docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md's release checklist, next to the existing version-bump / bin.lore-flip / tag / dispatch sequence. That edit is blocked until LCLI-468 reconciles this checkout onto the rebuilt origin history — editing docs now would mean committing on the pre-purge history. Do the docs change after LCLI-468, driven through lore per CLAUDE.md, with lore check exiting 0 as the definition of done.

acceptanceCriteria.text: docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md release checklist names the step: notify opum-marketplace with the new tag and the resolved skills/ tree SHA
The runbook states the passing case explicitly — re-tagging over byte-identical skills/ content needs no marketplace change

The concrete coupled files are named in the runbook (opum-marketplace scripts/check-federated-content.mjs and scripts/federated-pin-baselines.json), per the cross-repo-dependency rule that an unnamed concrete file is invisible to whoever deletes it

implementationNotes:
DELIVERED IN PR #87 (branch docs/LCLI-469-marketplace-tag-notification), as the last pre-tag item that fires ON the tag rather than after it. Cited by PR number rather than merge SHA, which is knowable before the merge.

THE STEP IS NOW IN THE RUNBOOK at docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md section "3. Cut a release", attached to item 4 -- the tag step -- rather than to the publish step. That placement is the decision: the notification fires when the tag exists, so item 6 would have been late.

THE BLOCKER IS GONE. This task recorded itself as blocked until LCLI-468 reconciled the checkout onto the rebuilt origin history. That reconciliation landed on 2026-09-10, so the edit is made on the correct history.

WHY IT WAS DECIDED NOW AND NOT DISCOVERED AFTER TAGGING, with the evidence:

  opum-marketplace's recorded baseline for opum-lore: 24277e9a94d6cc9b5a8c7fa12fa32c4f15eb4c0f
  skills/ tree at v0.6.2:                            24277e9a94d6cc9b5a8c7fa12fa32c4f15eb4c0f
  skills/ tree at dev (2026-09-15, pre-0.7.0 tag):   2998f74d077845f8ad73f83aa296e37e034378a4

skills/lore/SKILL.md gained 13 lines between v0.6.2 and the 0.7.0 tag candidate, so the resolved subtree SHA HAS moved. This release is the non-passing case: opum-marketplace's check-federated-content.mjs will go red on v0.7.0 unless their pin bump to that tag carries the re-resolved baseline in the SAME change. That is a fact, not a possibility, and it is exactly what this task existed to stop being found downstream as a red check.

The notification itself is not sent yet and cannot be: it carries the tag object SHA and the commit it peels to, neither of which exists until the tag is cut. The runbook now makes sending it a step of cutting the tag, which is the durable fix; sending it for v0.7.0 specifically is a one-time act tracked on LCLI-496 alongside the tag.

THE PASSING CASE IS WRITTEN DOWN TOO, and it is the common one: the baseline records a CONTENT SHA, not a tag, so a new tag over byte-identical skills/ resolves to the same value and their check stays green untouched. The runbook says to send the values anyway -- confirming a no-op costs one message -- and gives the `git diff --stat <previous-tag> <new-tag> -- skills/` that tells you which case you are in before you send.

BOTH CONCRETE FILES ARE NAMED in the runbook rather than referred to as "their federation check": opum-marketplace scripts/check-federated-content.mjs and scripts/federated-pin-baselines.json. Per the cross-repo-dependency rule, an abstract contract that never names the file implementing it is invisible to whoever deletes that file.

Validation: lore check exit 0 (78 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings), exit code taken without a pipe as the runbook itself requires. lore sync run before and after; docs/log.md regenerated with 0 unrecognized lines dropped.
